tx.t: This week we are studying the life of Marie Curie, one of the most important scientists of the twentieth century. She was born in Warsaw in eighteen sixty-seven and moved to Paris to study when she was twenty-four.

Together with her husband Pierre, she discovered two new elements, polonium and radium, in eighteen ninety-eight. In nineteen oh three she won the Nobel Prize in Physics, becoming the first woman ever to win a Nobel Prize.
In nineteen eleven she won a second Nobel Prize, this time in Chemistry. During the First World War, she developed mobile X-ray units that doctors used to treat wounded soldiers.
She died in nineteen thirty-four, probably because of her long exposure to radiation.

tx.t: Today I would like to outline what glaciers are, and why they matter for sea level. Glaciers cover about ten per cent of the world's land area.
Together, glaciers and ice sheets store about two thirds of the world's fresh water. A glacier forms when snow builds up for many years and is pressed into dense ice.
Since nineteen hundred, the global sea level has risen by about twenty centimetres. This rise is caused partly by melting ice and partly because warm water takes up more space.

It stretches for roughly two thousand three hundred kilometres. It is not one reef but a network of nearly three thousand individual reefs.
More than one thousand five hundred species of fish live there, together with many kinds of turtles and sharks. It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in nineteen eighty-one.
Warm water causes corals to expel the algae that feed them, which turns them white. This is called bleaching.

The famous Gutenberg Bible was printed around fourteen fifty-five. William Caxton set up the first printing press in England in fourteen seventy-six.
By the year fifteen hundred, historians estimate that more than twenty million books had been printed in Europe. Cheaper books helped literacy spread and made it easier to share new scientific ideas.

tx.t: Today I will explain how the human heart works. The heart has four chambers: two at the top, called atria, and two at the bottom, called ventricles.
At rest, the adult heart beats between sixty and one hundred times every minute. Over a day, that adds up to roughly one hundred thousand beats.
The heart pumps about five litres of blood around the body every minute. The heart of an adult weighs only about three hundred grams, and it is about the size of a clenched fist.
Regular exercise makes the heart stronger, so it can pump more blood with each beat.

In eighteen eighty-seven, the population was about five thousand. Over the next fifty years it grew to fifteen thousand.
Then things changed, because a large factory opened on the edge of town. As a result, most families moved to new houses nearby.
